name: Rhonda Vincent & The Rage
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 country-train — Rhonda Vincent & The Rage
notes: Contemporary hard-driving bluegrass with a country-radio-grade lead vocal. Two phrases are sourced directly and they are the whole model. The first is harmonic: the catalogue is documented as emphasising "progressive chord structures", which the entry translates as "I–IV–V plus real chromatic motion: secondary dominants (II7, VI7), a iv borrow, and passing diminished chords, which traditional bluegrass would not use". So the families carry I–VI–II–V, a I–iv–I–V borrow and a vii° passing family, `borrowed` names iv at 0.18, and `extensions.seventh` is 0.34 — the highest in this wing, because the stated II7 and VI7 are degree-plus-quality and this engine's numerals carry only the degree. The second is vocal: "multirange, fast-paced vocals" is glossed in the entry as "model a wide range (over an octave and a half) with high syllabic density — the opposite of the long-sustained-note bluegrass convention", so `melody.register` spans 29 semitones and `densityPerBar` is [6,12], the widest and busiest melody block in this section. The section states the rule this whole wing turns on: "the train beat is an ensemble function, not a drum part" — the banjo roll carries the continuous subdivision, the mandolin chop supplies the backbeat, and the upright bass supplies the two-beat kick. She plays mandolin herself, so "the chop is the lead instrument's part" — `snare.offGridMs` −6 for the driven placement, `kick` a flat 2 on anchors 1 and 3 for the upright, hat on quarters and not continuous, and `percs` on rim/shaker/triangle at −11 dB for the "brushed straight 8th stream at low velocity" the country-crossover cuts use. ⚠ The entry rates itself "medium-high on the vocal and harmonic parameters (both directly sourced as phrases); medium-low on tempo — no per-track readings were reachable, band inferred from the breakdown convention [LOW-CONF]". That flag applies to `bpm.mode` 170 inside the stated 130–210. ⚠ Also INFERRED: velocity tiers, `percs` contents, the countermelody and the bassline numbers.
